question: The primary goal of administering intravenous fluid therapy is to maintain or restore what body status?
explanation: IV fluids are directly introduced to correct deficits in body water and essential minerals quickly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why does intravenous administration create a faster therapeutic response than oral medication?

options.A: It bypasses the digestive system and enters the bloodstream directly
options.B: It increases the total volume of blood in circulation
options.C: It forces the heart to pump medications through the body faster
options.D: It activates the liver to process drugs without delay

explanation: Entering the venous system directly eliminates the time required for absorption through the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h1)

question: Normal saline solution with a concentration of 0.9% sodium chloride is classified as which type of fluid?
explanation: A 0.9% sodium chloride solution matches the solute concentration of normal blood plasma. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h2)

question: What physiological effect occurs when a hypertonic IV solution is infused into a patient?

options.A: Fluid moves out of the cells and into the bloodstream
options.B: Red blood cells absorb excess fluid and risk immediate rupture
options.C: Fluid shifts rapidly from the blood vessels into the body tissues
options.D: Water enters the cellular spaces to cause significant cell swelling

explanation: Higher solute concentration in hypertonic fluids creates osmotic pressure that pulls water out of cells. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h2)

question: How many drops per milliliter does a standard micro-drip infusion set deliver?
explanation: Micro-drip sets are calibrated to deliver sixty small drops to equal one exact milliliter of fluid. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h3)

question: When is a micro-drip infusion set preferred over a macro-drip set in clinical practice?

options.A: When infusing thick viscous blood products through a small peripheral vein
options.B: When delivering high volumes of isotonic saline to dehydrated adults
options.C: When rapidly replacing large volumes of blood lost during major surgery
options.D: When administering precise volumes to pediatric or critical care patients

explanation: The smaller drop size allows nurses to tightly control fluid delivery rates and prevent dangerous fluid overload. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h3)

question: Which venipuncture site should a nurse select first when initiating peripheral intravenous therapy on an adult?

options.A: Distal veins on the upper extremities
options.B: Large deep veins located in the lower extremities
options.C: Central veins accessed through the neck
options.D: Proximal veins close to the shoulder joint

explanation: Starting with distal veins preserves proximal venous sites for potential future therapy needs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h4)

question: Why must a nurse avoid placing an IV cannula in the arm of a patient who has had a mastectomy?

options.A: Blood pressure in that arm is permanently too high for accurate readings
options.B: The surgical scar prevents the tourniquet from wrapping securely
options.C: Impaired lymphatic drainage increases infection risk and lymphedema
options.D: Veins on that side of the body are completely absent after surgery

explanation: Lymph node removal disrupts fluid drainage, making the arm vulnerable to severe swelling and infection from punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h4)

question: At what angle should a nurse insert a peripheral IV catheter through the skin into the vein?
explanation: An insertion angle between 15 and 30 degrees allows the needle to safely pierce both skin and vein wall. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for allowing the skin antiseptic to dry completely before inserting the IV catheter?

options.A: It prevents the antiseptic from entering the bloodstream and causing toxicity
options.B: It hardens the outer layer of skin so the needle punctures more easily
options.C: It ensures the adhesive tape will stick firmly to the skin surface
options.D: It allows the chemical to complete its antimicrobial action and prevents burning

explanation: Antiseptics require time to destroy microorganisms, and wet chemicals can sting the patient during insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h5)

question: Electronic infusion pumps measure and deliver IV fluids using which unit of measurement?
explanation: Infusion pumps are programmed to deliver a precise hourly volume in milliliters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h6)

question: A patient's gravity infusion is running behind schedule. What action should the nurse take?

options.A: Open the roller clamp wide to catch up on the missed volume quickly
options.B: Recalculate the drop rate and adjust the roller clamp cautiously
options.C: Stop the infusion entirely and notify the physician immediately
options.D: Disconnect the tubing and flush the cannula with sterile water

explanation: Adjusting the rate gradually prevents sudden fluid overload, which can strain the cardiovascular system. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h6)

question: How often should a nurse typically inspect a peripheral IV insertion site during routine care?
explanation: Regular shift assessments allow for early detection of complications such as infiltration or phlebitis. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of flushing an intermittent peripheral IV lock with normal saline?

options.A: To test if the IV cannula is still securely attached to the skin
options.B: To cool down the vein and reduce local skin inflammation
options.C: To deliver an extra dose of hydration to the patient
options.D: To prevent blood from clotting inside the catheter lumen

explanation: Flushing clears residual blood from the cannula tip, keeping the pathway open for future medication administration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h7)

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of local phlebitis at an IV site?

options.A: A red, warm, and tender vein along the catheter path
options.B: Active bleeding leaking from beneath the transparent dressing
options.C: Cool, pale skin that is swollen around the insertion area
options.D: Sudden numbness and tingling in the fingers of that hand

explanation: Phlebitis involves inflammation of the vein wall, presenting with localized redness, warmth, and tenderness. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h8)

question: What is the first action a nurse must take when discovering an IV site has infiltrated?

options.A: Flush the line firmly with saline to clear the blockage
options.B: Increase the flow rate briefly to check vein patency
options.C: Stop the infusion and remove the catheter
options.D: Apply a warm compress directly over the swollen area

explanation: Stopping the infusion prevents more fluid from entering the surrounding tissue space. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h8)

question: Why must the nurse inspect the removed IV catheter tip after discontinuation?

options.A: To verify that the catheter tip is intact and no piece broke off inside the vein
options.B: To measure the exact length of the vein that was successfully cannulated
options.C: To determine if the cannula can be sterilized and reused for another patient
options.D: To check if any medication residue remains trapped inside the plastic tubing

explanation: Inspecting the removed tip ensures that a broken fragment did not break off and enter the bloodstream as an embolus. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h9)

question: How should a nurse withdraw a peripheral IV catheter from a patient's arm?

options.A: Pull the catheter out quickly while the tourniquet is tight
options.B: Lift the tip upward sharply as it leaves the vein
options.C: Pull it out smoothly and parallel to the skin surface
options.D: Twist the catheter gently to loosen it before pulling

explanation: Withdrawing parallel to the skin minimizes trauma to the vessel wall and reduces bruising. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h9)
